DOLFYN uses the Finite Volume Method with an own geometry format The geometric file (nodes, faces, volumes) with extension .dge is exported by SOFIMSHA. There are two principal variants:
 • The primary mesh uses the existing elements as cells. The solution is calculated for the centre of these cells. This is the standard procedure for the finite volume method.
 • The dual mesh is generated by a Voronoi-process based on the faces perpendicular on the element edges. The solution is then obtained for the nodes. The finite volumes are then polyhedra. This method has large benefits for the speed and precision for generated tetrahedra meshes in 3D.
 For spatial systems the BRIC-elements are taken directly. Surfaces have to be described via QUADs or structural areas.
 For planar systems SOFIMSHA will export for DOLFYN all QUAD-Elements as hexahedra with a thickenss of 1.0, the Volume-Patch number is generated from the properties of the QUAD.  DOLFYN boundary conditions are given for a total surface or a volume only, adressed by a unique region number. When exporting the mesh the user the primary group number will be used for this region number.

The leftmost “Record” column shows the record keyword; the right “Items” column lists allowed fields in that record (often in fixed order or as optional fields depending on the program rules).

### Record: FLOW
Contains items controlling fluid/flow or dynamic boundary-related parameters:
- **TURB** (turbulence), **TEMP** (temperature), **MAT** (material), **RHO** (density), **NUE** (kinematic viscosity)
- **TREF** (reference temperature), **BET** (coupling/turbulence constant), **COND** (thermal conductivity), **CP** (specific heat), **K** (general coefficient)
- **TREF/BET/COND/CP/K** indicate thermal and flow property definitions.

### Record: WIND
Defines wind-related parameters and coordinate/shape settings:
- **LC** (load case index), **V** (wind velocity), **HREF** (reference height)
- **Z0**, **Z0M** (roughness lengths / reference elevations for profiles)
- **DX, DY, DZ** (offsets in x/y/z), **HG** (height/generation parameter)
- Additional profile constants: **C1**, **C2**, **HMAX** (max height)
This record mixes load selection (**LC**) with profile definition (e.g., **Z0/Z0M**) and geometry offsets.

### Record: CASE
Defines the structure of a “case” including identifiers and options:
- General: **LC**, **PLC** (possibly procedure/load combination), **U, V, W** (component values)
- **EPS** and **TEMP** (tolerance/relative value and temperature), **P** (pressure or scalar), **W** (additional component)
- Profile/limits/selection: **PREF**, **PREFIX, PREVY, PREZ** (likely naming/prefixes for output or result components)
- **DEN** (density), **K** (coefficient), **TITLE** (case title)
Overall, CASE combines numerical parameters, temperature/pressure-like values, and naming metadata.

### Record: IN, OUT, INOU
These records manage *input/output mapping* and selected quantities:
- **IN**: **NO** (quantity number/index), **LC**, **U, V, W**, **DEN**, **K**, **EPS**, **TEMP**
- **OUT**: **NO**, **F** (flag indicating output type/category)
- **INOU**: **NO**, **LC**, **P**, **DEN**, **K**, **EPS**, **TEMP**
They appear to select variables by index **NO** and optionally attach case identifiers (**LC**) and physical parameters (**P, DEN, K, EPS, TEMP**).

### Record: WALL
Specifies wall boundary conditions:
- **NO**, **Z0**, **U, V, W**, **TEMP**, **R**, **EPS**, **HFLX**
Includes **HFLX** (heat flux) and **R** (a resistance/roughness parameter), alongside velocity components and temperature.

### Record: DRAG
Contains aerodynamic drag-related geometry and coefficient terms:
- **VREF**, **HREF**, **AREF** (reference velocity/height/area), **AX, AY, AZ** (area projections or coefficients)
- **AXX, AYY, AZZ** (directional/axis-specific factors)
- **ALF** and **REFX/REFY/REFZ** (likely reference point coordinates or transformation references)

### Record: STEP
Controls solution stepping:
- **N** (step number/sequence), **T** (time or step parameter)
- **TFAK** (time factor), **DTM** (time increment/monitoring), **INT** (interval)
- **TOL** (tolerance), **FORD**/**TORD** (order/accuracy setting), **TO RD** shown as **TORD**
- Appears to define incremental progression and numerical control.

### Record: HIST
Defines history output sampling/intervals:
- **TYPE**, **FROM**, **TO**, **INC** (increment)
Used to specify which quantity types are tracked and over what range.

### Record: SOLV
Specifies solver settings:
- **VAR** (variables), **DIFF** (differencing/diffusion option), **BFAC** (background/scale factor)
- **SLIM** (solution limit), **WITH** (mode/option), **RELA** (relative control)
This record centralizes numerical scheme constraints.

These likely define degrees-of-freedom/origin mapping for subsequent entities (exact semantics depend on the broader manual, but the table indicates that **DOLF** relates to origin/origin selection via **Origi**).

This example (millau.dat) shows the evaluation of the stationary wind drag coefficients for a section of a bridge depending on the angle of attack. The section is taken from the Millau bridge in France (Width 27.75, Height 4.20 m), where results of a wind tunnel test are available for the construction stage and the final stage.
 The first difficulty is given by the selection of the inflow conditions for the wind. For the original project extended CFD studies for the terrain have been performed, for the CFD and wind tunnel we have to generalize the inflow. The wind tunnel report gave a turbulence intensity of 9-10 %. Assuming a roughness of 0.30 m and a height of the bridge deck of 200 m, we get a turbulence intensity of 9.4 %. The integral length scale is 81.0 m.
 For the service state wind shields have been added, which have been modelled in the wind tunnel with perforated plates with 50 % permeability. A perfect match of results should not be anticipated therefore.
 An other question is if one should model the wind tunnel model (scale 1:75) or the real struc- ture. In that case we used the real world dimensions, which is recommended by us in general.
 In that case a 2D-Analysis is performed. To select the analysis model properly one should take care of the parameters for some fundamental questions:
 • Distance of the section to the boundaries above and below. If one selects to small dis- tances, the blocking effect will disturb the pressures obtained considerably. It is recom- mended to block at most 4 % of the flow area, better is 1 to 2 %.
 Length of the area behind and the mesh density. If the mesh behind the section has a coarse mesh or is not long enough, vortices may not be modelled properly and the variation in time may not be obtained at all. Stationary mean values of the pressures may be obtained however in most cases with the k-ε-Turbulence model. The recommendation is to use an extension of 10 to 15 times the bridge width.
